note: Palatial: grand, like a palace.
Groundlings: the poorer playgoers who stood in front of the stage in Shakespeare’s theater. Hamlet calls them people who like noisy shows.
source: William Shakespeare, Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/100

anchor: beggars and rakers of the garbage
note: Rakers of the garbage: scavengers who sorted through rubbish.
Wilfully: on purpose, with deliberate intent.

anchor: the futile kick of a heifer
note: Futile: useless. A young cow’s kick does little harm; a stallion’s would.
A shod stallion is a male horse wearing iron shoes, a dangerous kicker.
Gall: bitterness. Also bile, a bitter fluid.
Vitriol: sulfuric acid, here bitter, burning hatred.

anchor: tell-tale reports purveyed to his ear
note: Purveyed: supplied. A tell-tale is an informer.

anchor: Squeak, one of his more cunning Corporals
note: Ship’s corporals were the master-at-arms’ assistants. Squeak is a nickname for his shrill voice.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Ship’s corporal”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Interlopers: people who push in where they have no right.
Implicit: unquestioning, absolutely trusting and obedient.

anchor: the petty persecutions heretofore adverted to
note: Adverted: referred, mentioned earlier. Heretofore: until now.
Foment: to stir up trouble.
Sundry: several. Contumelious: insulting. Epithets: name-calling phrases.

anchor: never suspected the veracity of these reports
note: Veracity: truthfulness, the quality of being accurate.
Raillery: good-natured teasing, here bitter jokes at his expense.
Patrolmen: men who police, here the master-at-arms and his men.
Depravity: moral corruption, wickedness that is deeply rooted.

anchor: action is taken upon surmise as upon certainty
note: Surmise: a guess. He acts on a hunch as if it were fact.
Inordinate: excessive. A usurer lends at an unreasonable, harsh rate of interest.
James writes that “the devils also believe, and tremble,” meaning even evil spirits know there is a God.
source: The Bible (King James Version), James 2:19, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: Ogres: man-eating giants of fairy tale. He made small things into monsters.

anchor: justified animosity into a sort of retributive righteousness
note: Animosity: strong dislike. Retributive: paying back for wrong.

anchor: The Pharisee is the Guy Fawkes
note: Guy Fawkes plotted in 1605 to blow up Parliament with gunpowder in the cellars below. The Pharisees were a Jewish sect Jesus often denounced as hypocrites.
Clandestine: secret, done in hiding to avoid notice.

anchor: to try the temper of the man
note: Temper: here the nature or toughness of a man.

anchor: peculiar conscience assigned to be the private mentor of Claggart
note: Mentor: a trusted adviser. His conscience guides him like a coach.
